Subject: Re: CFO01: Ford Client Committee - Strictly Private and Confidential



 


STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL


Dear all,


I hope you are all well. I write further to my last update on 5 August 2025, to provide you with a brief update on the following
 matters as they relate to the Ford NOx Emissions Litigation (the “Ford Litigation”), and the Pan-NOx Litigation generally (the “Litigation”):


·        
PDD Trial Preparation;

·        
Claimants Mechanical Expert;

·        
Quantum Trial and discontinuance;

·        
Change in personnel.

PDD Trial Preparation and final Pre-Trial Review


We are fast approaching the commencement of the PDD Trial, with the first day of trial listed for 13 October 2025, and the trial
 due to run until 19 December 2025.


Our skeleton argument was filed and served on 19 September, representing a mammoth undertaking by the entire Solicitor team and
 the barristers. The Ford specific annex to the skeleton argument was filed and served on 24 September. There was a slight extension to the Ford annex on account of the Defendants providing a very late second witness statement from a Ford employee. While we
 were not obliged to permit this into evidence, we took the view after considering it, that the statement was in fact more helpful for us and the case to allow its entry, rather than refusing permissions. As a caveat to our permittance of its inclusion, we
 agreed a short extension to the Ford annex.


As soon as I am in a position to provide you with a copy of the skeleton argument (with redactions for confidential information)
 I will send this to you. I would hope this will be later this week. I am extremely pleased with the final version of the skeleton argument. Our counsel team have done a remarkable job and it presents the best possible case for the court to consider.


While negotiations on the final timetable continue between the parties, we are close to concluding the timetable.


The first week of trial, due to commence on 13 October 2025, will consist of the Claimants and the Defendants making their opening
 remarks to the Court, in essence setting the scene, before we then move into evidence on what constitutes Normal Driving Conditions and then turning to each individual manufacturer. The order of the manufacturers will be Mercedes, Ford, Peugeot Citroen, Renault
 and Nissan.


It is expected that the Ford evidence, including the cross examination of experts and witnesses, will start on or around 13 November
 and run for just over a week.


If any of you are interested in attending Court for any part of the trial, please let us know and we will be able to arrange this
 with you.


There is due to be a final “Pre-Trial Review” hearing before the Court on 6 October which we are preparing for and this hearing
 will aim to settle any final issues or disputes that may impact the smooth running of the trial. The parties are in the process of agreeing an agenda for this hearing, and we will provide you with a further update on this in due course.


Claimants’ Software and Mechanical Experts


As per my previous update, I confirmed that in a hearing on 10 September, the Court unfortunately did not side with the Claimants
 in respect of the expert applications, and gave some strict directions with regard to steps the parties were required to take in respect of the software evidence that had been prepared.


We have been working hard to prepare and finalise the software report with the redactions / removals as advised by the Court and
 a version of these amended reports was provided to the Defendants on 24 September. We are awaiting the Defendants’ response to this draft report.  


In respect of the Claimants' mechanical expert, the Claimants' barrister team have provided a note to us in which they have flagged
 certain concerns with the mechanical expert. They have raised that they are concerned how the expert will perform at trial and that certain precautions need to be taken with the expert. Importantly, however, they have not told us that these concerns impact
 on the prospects of success of the case and we remain confident in the case we have prepared against Ford.


We are taking this note incredibly seriously and we are working hard, with the other Lead Solicitors, to prepare the expert for
 the trial. We are confident that, even with these concerns, the expert will be suitably prepared for trial, having undergone significant preparatory work before he takes the stand.


The expert is due to travel to the UK, from America, on 29 September, and will largely be based here, with the team, until his
 evidence is complete. He will observe various cross-examinations of other experts and will get a good feel for the experience he is likely to have in the witness box.


The team will also be assisting him in his preparation.


If you have any questions regarding this, please do let me and the Ford team know.


Quantum Trial


As you are aware, the Court has ordered that a second trial be listed in these NOx Litigations for October 2026. This trial, referred
 to as the “Quantum Trial” is in relation to the value of certain claims that are being brought by the Claimants. The Court will assess what value should be attributed to different heads of loss claimed by the Claimants, each of which were sustained as a result
 of the Defendants’ conduct, and determine a value for each claim being brought.


The Quantum Trial is proceeding, at least initially, on the basis of assumptions that the vehicles had prohibited defeat devices
 in them. This is necessary because we will not have a judgment from the Court on the defeat devices until at some point in mid-2026 (post the October 2025 trial), and it is impractical for the entire litigation to grind to a half while waiting for this judgment.
 As such, we will prepare evidence and submissions on what we have pleaded for the PDD Trial, and this will then be updated, in very short order, once we have that judgment.


It is obviously impractical for the Court to hear evidence and consider losses on an individual basis (to do so would defeat the
 purpose of a group litigation), and so how this trial will proceed is by way of Sample Claimants. These are Claimants, selected between the Claimants and Defendants, who represent a range of characteristics and different issues across the Claimant cohort such
 that findings by the Court can be applied to all claimants. The characteristics that the Claimants needed to represent were included in Annex 2 to the October 2024 CMC Order, a copy of which is attached again for ease.


The process of negotiating these Sample Claimants took some time but the parties have finally reach agreement. A total of 40 Sample
 Claimants have been negotiated between the Claimants and Defendants across the Pan-NOx Litigations, split as eight per manufacturer, and of those eight, four selected by the Claimants, and four by the Defendants. Details of the Ford Sample Claimants can be
 provided if required.


Over the course of the negotiations, the Defendants made various nominations that the Claimants wished to resist, for various reasons
 i.e. the Claimants did not wish to participate as Sample Claimants, or they wished to pursue their claim in a different jurisdiction. In circumstances where those Sample Claimant nominees did not wish to proceed, the Defendants have taken the position that
 they must have their claims removed from the English Litigation. We have some sympathy with this, especially where Claimants wish to pursue their claim in a different jurisdiction.


Kenneth Gormley is one such person. Mr Gormley is a Ford Claimant, was nominated by the Defendants as a Sample Claimant, however
 we have since identified he is bringing a claim in both the England & Wales jurisdiction as part of this claim, and also in a separate litigation in Scotland.


Mr Gormley cannot continue with both claims and he was required to pick which one he wanted to continue with and we have instructions
 from Mr Gormley that he wishes to pursue his claim as part of the Scottish proceedings. We therefore are required to prepare and serve a formal notice of discontinuance in respect of Mr Gormley’s claim in the English proceedings.


Pursuant to paragraphs 29 and 30 of the Ford Group Litigation Order, we are seeking your instructions to act on Mr Gormley’s instructions
 and discontinue his claim.


Before confirming these instructions, we must advise you of the effect of this discontinuance. While it will not adversely impact
 the litigation, indeed the Litigation is already proceeding past this, the discontinuance will necessarily result in the Defendants being entitled to incur costs in the Litigation, that will be recoverable by them in due course.

De-designation Hearing
(“DDH”)


One key hurdle the parties face in these Pan-NOx Litigations is that there are significant barriers erected between the Litigations
 that prevent the efficient and effective exchange and comparison of information and disclosure between the cases. This is a fundamental part of the Claimants claim i.e. that many of the manufacturers were either sharing strategies and technology to insert
 prohibits defeat devices (“PDDs”) in their vehicles, or alternatively, that better technology was available that was being used by other manufacturers that mean the Defendants did not need to insert PDDs in their vehicles.


As mentioned in previous updates, much the information that exists in the Ford Litigation, and similarly in the other Lead Cases
 (Mercedes, Renault/Nissan and Peugeot Citroën) is subject to a case specific Confidentiality Ring Orders (“CRO”). Each of the Lead cases has their own CRO. The Defendants have taken this CRO as a means to try and keep secret the majority of the documentation
 that they have provided to us, thereby restricting access to the documents to persons who are members of the CRO. Despite protestations from the Defendants, we have successfully implemented a Pan-Lead CRO, which has been constructed to assist in the sharing
 of confidential information across the cases. While this is helpful in permitted us to see documents from other cases, it does not alleviate the issue of transferring documents into the Pan-Lead CRO (as the Defendants continue to raise various issues regarding
 this) and it does not prevent those documents being confidential and only certain people being able to see them. This does not go to the principle of open justice, whereby the public should know the conduct of these manufacturers. It is and always has been
 our intention to seek to de-designate these documents so that they can be referred to openly and in public.


The DDH is shaped at doing precisely that; bringing those documents into the public and also to make the process of hearing these
 cases in court more feasible. Under present circumstances, any time a party wishes to discuss any documentation that is confidential, it would require the Court room to be emptied of people who are not within the CROs, which is simply unworkable. The DDH is
 intended to allow open justice to be carried out. 


The Claimants prepared and filed their respective applications and witness evidence on 13 June 2025 and we took receipt of the
 Defendants’ responsive evidence late last night. We are considering this with our counsel team in advance of the preparation of skeleton arguments and the hearing itself.

STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL


Dear all,


I hope you are all well. I write further to my last update on 5 August 2025, to provide you with a brief update on the following
 matters as they relate to the Ford NOx Emissions Litigation (the “Ford Litigation”), and the Pan-NOx Litigation generally (the “Litigation”):


·       
PDD Trial Preparation;

·       
Claimants Mechanical Expert;

·       
Quantum Trial and discontinuance;

·       
Change in personnel.

PDD Trial Preparation and final Pre-Trial Review


We are fast approaching the commencement of the PDD Trial, with the first day of trial listed for 13 October 2025, and the trial
 due to run until 19 December 2025.


Our skeleton argument was filed and served on 19 September, representing a mammoth undertaking by the entire Solicitor team and
 the barristers. The Ford specific annex to the skeleton argument was filed and served on 24 September. There was a slight extension to the Ford annex on account of the Defendants providing a very late second witness statement from a Ford employee. While we
 were not obliged to permit this into evidence, we took the view after considering it, that the statement was in fact more helpful for us and the case to allow its entry, rather than refusing permissions. As a caveat to our permittance of its inclusion, we
 agreed a short extension to the Ford annex.


As soon as I am in a position to provide you with a copy of the skeleton argument (with redactions for confidential information)
 I will send this to you. I would hope this will be later this week. I am extremely pleased with the final version of the skeleton argument. Our counsel team have done a remarkable job and it presents the best possible case for the court to consider.


While negotiations on the final timetable continue between the parties, we are close to concluding the timetable.


The first week of trial, due to commence on 13 October 2025, will consist of the Claimants and the Defendants making their opening
 remarks to the Court, in essence setting the scene, before we then move into evidence on what constitutes Normal Driving Conditions and then turning to each individual manufacturer. The order of the manufacturers will be Mercedes, Ford, Peugeot Citroen, Renault
 and Nissan.


It is expected that the Ford evidence, including the cross examination of experts and witnesses, will start on or around 13 November
 and run for just over a week.


If any of you are interested in attending Court for any part of the trial, please let us know and we will be able to arrange this
 with you.


There is due to be a final “Pre-Trial Review” hearing before the Court on 6 October which we are preparing for and this hearing
 will aim to settle any final issues or disputes that may impact the smooth running of the trial. The parties are in the process of agreeing an agenda for this hearing, and we will provide you with a further update on this in due course.


Claimants’ Software and Mechanical Experts


As per my previous update, I confirmed that in a hearing on 10 September, the Court unfortunately did not side with the Claimants
 in respect of the expert applications, and gave some strict directions with regard to steps the parties were required to take in respect of the software evidence that had been prepared.


We have been working hard to prepare and finalise the software report with the redactions / removals as advised by the Court and
 a version of these amended reports was provided to the Defendants on 24 September. We are awaiting the Defendants’ response to this draft report.  


In respect of the Claimants' mechanical expert, the Claimants' barrister team have provided a note to us in which they have flagged
 certain concerns with the mechanical expert. They have raised that they are concerned how the expert will perform at trial and that certain precautions need to be taken with the expert. Importantly, however, they have not told us that these concerns impact
 on the prospects of success of the case and we remain confident in the case we have prepared against Ford.


We are taking this note incredibly seriously and we are working hard, with the other Lead Solicitors, to prepare the expert for
 the trial. We are confident that, even with these concerns, the expert will be suitably prepared for trial, having undergone significant preparatory work before he takes the stand.


The expert is due to travel to the UK, from America, on 29 September, and will largely be based here, with the team, until his
 evidence is complete. He will observe various cross-examinations of other experts and will get a good feel for the experience he is likely to have in the witness box.


The team will also be assisting him in his preparation.


If you have any questions regarding this, please do let me and the Ford team know.


Quantum Trial


As you are aware, the Court has ordered that a second trial be listed in these NOx Litigations for October 2026. This trial, referred
 to as the “Quantum Trial” is in relation to the value of certain claims that are being brought by the Claimants. The Court will assess what value should be attributed to different heads of loss claimed by the Claimants, each of which were sustained as a result
 of the Defendants’ conduct, and determine a value for each claim being brought.


The Quantum Trial is proceeding, at least initially, on the basis of assumptions that the vehicles had prohibited defeat devices
 in them. This is necessary because we will not have a judgment from the Court on the defeat devices until at some point in mid-2026 (post the October 2025 trial), and it is impractical for the entire litigation to grind to a half while waiting for this judgment.
 As such, we will prepare evidence and submissions on what we have pleaded for the PDD Trial, and this will then be updated, in very short order, once we have that judgment.


It is obviously impractical for the Court to hear evidence and consider losses on an individual basis (to do so would defeat the
 purpose of a group litigation), and so how this trial will proceed is by way of Sample Claimants. These are Claimants, selected between the Claimants and Defendants, who represent a range of characteristics and different issues across the Claimant cohort such
 that findings by the Court can be applied to all claimants. The characteristics that the Claimants needed to represent were included in Annex 2 to the October 2024 CMC Order, a copy of which is attached again for ease.


The process of negotiating these Sample Claimants took some time but the parties have finally reach agreement. A total of 40 Sample
 Claimants have been negotiated between the Claimants and Defendants across the Pan-NOx Litigations, split as eight per manufacturer, and of those eight, four selected by the Claimants, and four by the Defendants. Details of the Ford Sample Claimants can be
 provided if required.


Over the course of the negotiations, the Defendants made various nominations that the Claimants wished to resist, for various reasons
 i.e. the Claimants did not wish to participate as Sample Claimants, or they wished to pursue their claim in a different jurisdiction. In circumstances where those Sample Claimant nominees did not wish to proceed, the Defendants have taken the position that
 they must have their claims removed from the English Litigation. We have some sympathy with this, especially where Claimants wish to pursue their claim in a different jurisdiction.


Kenneth Gormley is one such person. Mr Gormley is a Ford Claimant, was nominated by the Defendants as a Sample Claimant, however
 we have since identified he is bringing a claim in both the England & Wales jurisdiction as part of this claim, and also in a separate litigation in Scotland.


Mr Gormley cannot continue with both claims and he was required to pick which one he wanted to continue with and we have instructions
 from Mr Gormley that he wishes to pursue his claim as part of the Scottish proceedings. We therefore are required to prepare and serve a formal notice of discontinuance in respect of Mr Gormley’s claim in the English proceedings.


Pursuant to paragraphs 29 and 30 of the Ford Group Litigation Order, we are seeking your instructions to act on Mr Gormley’s instructions
 and discontinue his claim.


Before confirming these instructions, we must advise you of the effect of this discontinuance. While it will not adversely impact
 the litigation, indeed the Litigation is already proceeding past this, the discontinuance will necessarily result in the Defendants being entitled to incur costs in the Litigation, that will be recoverable by them in due course.


As an initial reassurance, these costs will not be due from you or from any of the Claimants, but they will instead be covered,
 should they need to be paid, by either the ATE provider who is providing cover for this Litigation, or by Mr Gormley himself.


The general rule, under the governing Civil Procedure Rules 38.6 is that where a Claimant discontinues all or part of their claim,
 the Defendant has an automatic right to the costs they have incurred in respect of their claim.


There will be two types of costs that the Defendants will be able to recover: common costs, and individual costs.


As explained in the Client Committee meeting post the first Cost Management Hearing, the individual costs will be costs solely
 in relation to Mr Gormley’s claim, and the common costs will be the apportioned share of the Defendants overall costs of this exercise in relation to Mr Gormley’s claim. Mr Gormley’s claim is one claim out of hundreds of thousands, and so while we remain unaware
 of the level of costs that have been incurred by the Defendants, we believe the overall amount of the common costs will be minimal.


These costs cannot be resolved until the conclusion of the case and so there is no immediate cost that will be required to be paid.


I am of course available to discuss any aspect of this with you before you confirm your instructions, but I wish to reassure you
 that this discontinuance will not result in you, or any of the other thousands of claimants in the Litigation, being out of pocket.

De-designation Hearing
(“DDH”)


One key hurdle the parties face in these Pan-NOx Litigations is that there are significant barriers erected between the Litigations
 that prevent the efficient and effective exchange and comparison of information and disclosure between the cases. This is a fundamental part of the Claimants claim i.e. that many of the manufacturers were either sharing strategies and technology to insert
 prohibits defeat devices (“PDDs”) in their vehicles, or alternatively, that better technology was available that was being used by other manufacturers that mean the Defendants did not need to insert PDDs in their vehicles.


As mentioned in previous updates, much the information that exists in the Ford Litigation, and similarly in the other Lead Cases
 (Mercedes, Renault/Nissan and Peugeot Citroën) is subject to a case specific Confidentiality Ring Orders (“CRO”). Each of the Lead cases has their own CRO. The Defendants have taken this CRO as a means to try and keep secret the majority of the documentation
 that they have provided to us, thereby restricting access to the documents to persons who are members of the CRO. Despite protestations from the Defendants, we have successfully implemented a Pan-Lead CRO, which has been constructed to assist in the sharing
 of confidential information across the cases. While this is helpful in permitted us to see documents from other cases, it does not alleviate the issue of transferring documents into the Pan-Lead CRO (as the Defendants continue to raise various issues regarding
 this) and it does not prevent those documents being confidential and only certain people being able to see them. This does not go to the principle of open justice, whereby the public should know the conduct of these manufacturers. It is and always has been
 our intention to seek to de-designate these documents so that they can be referred to openly and in public.


The DDH is shaped at doing precisely that; bringing those documents into the public and also to make the process of hearing these
 cases in court more feasible. Under present circumstances, any time a party wishes to discuss any documentation that is confidential, it would require the Court room to be emptied of people who are not within the CROs, which is simply unworkable. The DDH is
 intended to allow open justice to be carried out. 


The Claimants prepared and filed their respective applications and witness evidence on 13 June 2025 and we took receipt of the
 Defendants’ responsive evidence late last night. We are considering this with our counsel team in advance of the preparation of skeleton arguments and the hearing itself.

To: Ford Litigation Team <fordteam@pogustgoodhead.com>
Subject: Looking Ford-ward 
 






Team,




Over the last few days post the Lead Solicitor application, I and the other case leads, have been engaging with LD to establish what our
brave new world will look like and how the teams implement it. 




Ultimately, whether we like it or not (and barring the Court going completely left field in their judgment tomorrow), LD are going to be the sole Lead Solicitor on the Ford Litigation. I am genuinely sorry that this has happened and that things have happened
 the way that they have. None of you deserve to the subject to this. This juncture has been reached through no fault of any of yours and believe me when I say I know just how unpleasant it feels. I also fully appreciate that it sucks even more to know that,
 despite how much it feels like we've been relegated to "just another claimant firm", we will still need to perform largely the same role that we have been before now - except we do it without the title of Lead Solicitor.  




As we try to gather some understanding of how this new world will practically work, especially with the Agency Agreement that the firms have executed, there are a few things that look to have been decided that I can inform you of:





The AA (as the firms have executed) puts me under the supervision of LD - it does not extend to you as individuals. You will still work under PG and your day jobs go on as normal. How this works for me and my
 instructions to you, we are all trying to get to the bottom of. You are all smart lawyers and I am sure you can appreciate that I may have some concerns over how this works in practice, but I (and the other case leads) will be doing what we can to a) ensure
 you are fully equipped and supported to do you job and b) find a solution that works for everyone so we can move forward;

LD will take over all comms (incoming and outgoing) to the Ds. As part of the AA that the firms have agreed, I will be CC'ed on those emails, and I will then need to pass them onto the team along with instructions;

Similar with external meetings with the Defendants. The de facto is that LD will attend these solo but there will inevitably be instances where PG team members are needed;

Communications with counsel etc can (I believe) proceed as normal and we shouldn't have to run these past LD, but if that changes, I will let you know;

All external work on the PG SharePoint that is "common work" will at some stage be moved over to the LD SharePoint - this is to ensure links going out to the Ds etc go from a Leigh Day email account (the timeline
 on this is very much TBC becuase of how big of a task it is);

Group Register (and Notice of Objection) work has not yet been decided but §19 of the Ford GLO dictates that PG have responsibility for this, not the Lead Solicitor, so it is likely that this will remain as
 it has been. I will update on this when I know more;

Trial preparation and attendance is expected to be as it would have been otherwise. I have been today working on a rota for who will be where, when. There is also a suggestion that we may work from LD for the
 week(s) before the trial to make preparation and communication easier. This sounds like a very good idea to me and I will update on this when I know more.





It's not all doom and gloom. The entire LD team, especially the LD Ford team and Nichola in particular, know how difficult a time this is for us collectively and all of you as individuals. They are immensely appreciative of all of the work that we are doing
 and they understand that collaboration between us must continue elsewise there is every chance things will fall over. 




We will keep plugging on and I will keep you all as informed as I can over the coming days and weeks. One piece of good news (if you choose to take it as good news) is that I will be in the office almost weekly from now until I depart for my new role, starting
 from next week. We have opening submissions on Monday and Tuesday - let's arrange to do a team lunch, or heaven forbid a drink post-work, one of the days next week to celebrate having got this insanely massive piece of litigation to trial within 2 years of
 making the GLO application - that in itself is insane never mind what we have been through over the last 2 years (and 2 months). I say this often, but I am genuinely astonished at how freakishly competent you all are at your jobs and I am very very proud to
 work alongside all of you. You are all an absolute credit.




As always, I'm around if anyone wants to chat or discuss anything in the email.




Thanks,




Michael
